walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity & Conservation — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity & Conservation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity & Conservation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: MacArthur and Wilson published island biogeography theory in:
IUCN Red List category 'EN' stands for:
options: Endemic
Endangered
Environmental
Extinct in nature

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Because warming is positive (a good thing).
Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Water bubbling up from underground.
Because plants only use carbon.
Water bubbling up from underground.
Water flowing through soil into rivers.
Water vapour released from plant leaves to the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Because plants only use carbon.
Water bubbling up from underground.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
